item.title: Musk's TeraFab dream meets Nvidia reality check on chip manufacturing limits
item.description: Elon Musk's ambition to build a massive in-house semiconductor manufacturing complex has drawn fresh caution from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who stressed that advanced chip production ranks among the most technically demanding industrial undertakings globally—far beyond the reach of capital spending alone.

item.title: Morris Chang resurfaces as Jensen Huang returns to Taipei
item.description: TSMC founder Morris Chang made his first public appearance in more than a year on January 29, 2026, dining with Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang just hours after Huang arrived in Taipei.

item.title: CIP completes first subsea foundations for Fengmiao wind farm, on track for 2027 completion
item.description: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP), through its fifth flagship fund Copenhagen Infrastructure V (CI V), held a milestone event on January 29, 2026, at Taipei Port to showcase the completion of the first batch of subsea foundation assemblies for the Fengmiao Offshore Wind Farm. The project is on track for full completion in 2027.

item.title: China claims 64% of ESS battery market as South Korea scrambles to launch a comeback
item.description: The global energy storage system (ESS) market based on lithium-ion batteries expanded in 2025. According to ET News and Ddaily, SNE Research reported that global shipments of lithium-ion batteries for ESS by manufacturers totaled 550 GWh in 2025, up 79% from 307 GWh in 2024, reflecting strong growth momentum. item.title: Taiwan's capital markets reach new highs, signaling broader global role
item.description: At a Lunar New Year press conference, the Financial Supervisory Commission said that combined revenues of Taiwan's listed companies surpassed NT$50 trillion (approx. US$1.59 trillion) in 2025, while total market capitalization reached NT$101 trillion. By market value, Taiwan now ranks as the world's seventh-largest securities market.

item.title: Century Group secures over NT$100 billion in wind power orders
item.description: The draft rules for vendor selection in offshore wind power Phase 3-3 have, for the first time, removed localization requirements. However, this has not slowed investment in Taiwan by companies including Century Iron & Steel. Because localization requirements impact domestic suppliers that have already made substantial investments, Century Group calls for a gradual policy adjustment. item.title: Samsung, SK Hynix target surging growth in automotive memory market for autonomous driving systems
item.description: Automobiles are rapidly transforming into servers/smartphones-on-wheels with the advancement of autonomous driving technologies, which has led to a surge in demand for automotive memory. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are viewing the automotive sector as the next major battleground after AI, with both South Korean memory giants taking proactive measures to gain a foothold in this emerging market.

item.title: LG Display plans KRW 2 trillion OLED investment in 2026, but holds back on next-gen IT panels
item.description: LG Display, fresh off its first profitable year in four years, is preparing to step up investment in 2026 as it seeks to strengthen its position in the increasingly competitive OLED market. Despite that, the company is proceeding cautiously on one of the industry's most closely watched questions: whether and when to commit to large-scale production of next-generation OLED panels for IT devices.

item.title: Shenzhen Ingchips joins domestic chipmakers in raising prices as cost pressures mount
item.description: Shenzhen Ingchips Technology has joined Goke Microelectronics and Cmsemicon in announcing price increases, highlighting mounting cost pressures across China's semiconductor supply chain.

item.title: Intel signals return to memory with new DRAM bonding research
item.description: In early 2026, a research update published by Sandia National Laboratories (SNL), part of the US Department of Energy, sparked industry discussions about whether Intel is poised to re-enter the DRAM market. Although the report did not explicitly confirm Intel's large-scale comeback in DRAM manufacturing, the signals it released warrant consideration.
